business_profile.business_name: Millet Milling and Value-Added Products Processing Unit
business_profile.sub_category: Millets Primary and Secondary Processing and Value Addition
business_profile.business_model: Micro and Small Food Processing - Custom milling + branded value-added products (flour, rava, flakes, ready-to-cook mixes, rotti, cookies)
business_profile.description: Unit that cleans, grades, dehulls, destones, mills jowar, bajra, ragi, foxtail, little, kodo, barnyard, proso into rice, flour, rava, flakes and value-added products like rotti, papad, cookies, laddu. Suitable for rural areas of Kalaburagi where jowar area is 100482 ha with production 134829 tonnes (Selco Foundation scoping study) and district is 90% rainfed with jowar-bajra staple. Leverages Kalaburagi Rotti SHG model, FPO network (Aland Bhootai Millets FPC, Jewargi Taluka Millets FPC), APMC Gulbarga which trades Bajra, Jowar, Tur.

rural_suitability.reason: High local raw material availability (jowar/bajra), 90% rainfed millet culture, existing SHG/FPO processing initiatives, APMC infrastructure handling jowar/bajra, low power requirement, supported by Karnataka millet processing 50% subsidy up to 10 lakh and PMFME 35% subsidy.

comparison_table.Jevargi/Jewargi: Medium (tur/cotton dominant, APMC not listing jowar)

taluk_comparison.recommendation_reason: Kalaburagi taluk has verified high demand via Kalaburagi Rotti cooperative (1000 women, Rs 50 lakh revenue, Amazon, export US/Canada/Australia), APMC Gulbarga trading Bajra/Jowar modal Rs 4250/qtl, 100482 ha jowar production 134829 tonnes, NABARD-CFTRI FT-CFC tech support, 50% state millet processing subsidy up to 10 lakh, 90% rainfed jowar/bajra staple. seasonality.peak_period: Dec-Feb (rabi jowar harvest) and Oct-Nov (festive demand, millet enclave, Krishi Mela Nov)
seasonality.low_period: June-August (monsoon, low arrivals, sowing period 4.69% in Kalaburagi taluk June)
seasonality.reason: Jowar is rabi crop (rabi season trials in Afzalpur Mannur etc), bajra kharif Sep-Oct; storage allows year-round milling but lean months require stock; Krishi Mela Nov focuses millets; Rotti demand stable daily but peaks winter
seasonality.business_impact: Raw material price lowest post-harvest Dec-Feb (Rs 3000/qtl) vs lean Rs 4850-5500/qtl; revenue stable due to daily rotti staple; utilization can drop if no storage
mitigation: Use HDPE bins and godown facility subsidized up to Rs 50 lakh per FO
Diversify to ragi (sourced state-wide) and minor millets
Offer custom milling service at nominal charge per RKVY evaluation to maintain capacity

climate_factors: Rainfall reduction in NIK including Kalaburagi per IMD climate study 1964-1990 vs 1991 onwards
Drought 2023 Krishi Mela focus on drought-resistant varieties
climate_and_climate_change.climate_change_risk: Medium-High - NIK rainfall reduced, deficit reported 14 districts including Kalaburagi Oct 2025 KSNDMC; late monsoon slowed sowing 2019
climate_and_climate_change.business_impact: Low direct impact on milling (indoor) but high indirect via raw material availability and price; transport disruption during heavy rain (IMD heavy rain predicted Kalaburagi)
mitigation_measures: Source from multiple taluks and districts (Bidar, Raichur, Vijayapura major jowar districts per agricultural journals)
Solar-powered unit as per SELCO-NABARD Balangir model reduces power risk
Drought-resistant millet varieties promoted under Raitha Siri
adaptation_strategy: Promote Raitha Siri incentive Rs 10000/ha to expand area - supply security
CFTRI standardized processes for low-moisture grains
Diversify to value-added with longer shelf life (cookies, papad)

assumptions.source/basis: Small millet unit 290 days per Model DPR
APMC Kalaburagi modal 3000-3500-4250 per KisanDeals and CommodityMarketLive
Retail premium over grain 60-80% (grain Rs 35-45/kg flour Rs 70)
Kodo millet DPR 90% recovery, sorghum flakes 60% - use 85% for jowar flour
Kalaburagi Rotti initiative - procured at Rs 5-6 sold at Rs 7

financial_model.calculation_methodology: Monthly Revenue = kg milled * recovery * selling price; Example small: 100kg/day * 25 days * 0.85 recovery * Rs 70 = 148750 plus custom milling charges 300 kg/day * Rs 3/kg *25=22500 total ~171250 expected. Expenses = Raw material 2.5MT*35000=87500 + labour 15000 + electricity 2000 + packaging 8000 + transport 5000 + maintenance 3000 = ~116500 expected. Conservative 60% capacity, optimistic 140% capacity. Break-even = Initial Investment / Monthly Operating Profit: 850000/60000=14 months.

strengths: High local raw material: Kalaburagi jowar 100482 ha 134829 tonnes plus bajra staple 90% rainfed
Proven market model: Kalaburagi Rotti 1000 women, 100 machines, Rs 50 lakh revenue, Amazon/exports
Institutional support: NABARD-CFTRI FT-CFC MoA for 7 districts, technology transfer, SOPs
Government subsidy: Karnataka 50% up to 10 lakh for millet processing units + PMFME 35% up to 10 lakh
weaknesses: Low productivity: Kalaburagi remains deficit district despite 206682 ha sorghum due to low yield 1379 kg/ha needing tech intervention
Power and water: Rural 3-phase intermittent, groundwater dependent (CGWB aquifer 1843 sq km Jevargi)
Limited minor millet local supply - Karnataka minor millets only 0.31 lakh ha
High initial civil cost Rs 400/sqft per Model DPR
opportunities: Millet mainstreaming 24% PDS ragi/jowar distribution, millet hub single-window per Budget 2026-27, Raitha Siri Rs 10000/ha incentive
e-commerce: ONDC, GeM, FPO Kisan Bazar already used by Aland FPC; Rotti franchise to Bengaluru/Hyderabad/Pune
Value addition: Rava/flaking jowar, popping ragi, parboiling pearl millet, cookies (Karnataka DSA Kodo millet cookies DPR)
Solar-powered processing unit NABARD-SELCO model Balangir reducing cost and diesel dependence
threats: Crop shift: Sugarcane retained 40% area and gained 38% from jowar and 21% from Bengal gram in Kalaburagi transition matrix
Climate: NIK rainfall reduction, Kalaburagi deficit 14 districts Oct 2025 KSNDMC, late monsoon slowed sowing
Price competition: APMC jowar modal Rs 3000-4250/qtl, branded flour premium may be undercut by unorganized chakki
Quality: Without destoner, stones/mud balls identical to grain size - food safety risk

seven_day_validation_experiment.objective: Validate millet milling demand, supply, pricing in chosen taluk before investing Rs 8.5 lakh small scale

days.activity: Visit APMC Gulbarga Nehru Gunj and Jewargi/Chittapur markets, note jowar/bajra arrivals, modal price, interview 5 commission agents
days.measurement: Price range Rs 3000-5500/qtl verified, arrivals quintals/day

days.activity: Interview potential customers: 10 households, 2 hotels, 1 mid-day meal supplier, 5 existing SHG rotti makers
days.measurement: Willingness to pay flour Rs 60-80/kg, rotti Rs 7, repeat purchase intention %

days.activity: Contact suppliers: 3 machinery suppliers (Perfura Coimbatore Rs 92500 destoner, Nabhitha Hyderabad dehuller 96k-225k, Meet Machines Indore 327k 500kg/hr), 2 packaging vendors
Test product: Procure 50kg jowar from Aland Bhootai FPC, custom mill at existing mill, make flour and 20 rottis with SHG women
days.measurement: Recovery %, rotti quality, time per kg, customer feedback score 1-5

days.activity: Attempt actual sales/pre-orders: Sell trial flour 20kg at Rs 70/kg door-to-door, list on local WhatsApp group, take 5 rotti pre-orders
days.measurement: Number of paid orders, rejection rate, acquisition cost

days.activity: Calculate unit economics: Revenue 20kg*70=1400 minus grain 20/0.85*35=823 minus expenses 200 = profit 377; scale to 100kg/day
days.measurement: Margin per kg, monthly profit projection vs expected Rs 60k

days.activity: Decision meeting with FPO leader and DIC officer; check PMFME portal eligibility and Raitha Siri 50% subsidy application
days.measurement: If >6 of 10 households interested, >3 pre-orders, margin >Rs 15/kg and subsidy applicable = Proceed; if 3-5 interest = Modify; <3 = Do Not Proceed

success_criteria: At least 6 of 10 households willing to buy millet flour regularly
At least 3 machinery quotations within Rs 4-5 lakh small scale
Trial recovery >=80% and rotti quality score >=4/5
At least 10kg paid sales on day 5
seven_day_validation_experiment.decision_rule: Proceed if success criteria >=4 met; Modify (reduce scale to custom milling service only) if 2-3 met; Do Not Proceed if <2 met

government_schemes.scheme_selection_method: Select the five most relevant currently applicable schemes based on verified business eligibility and financial relevance - PMFME for millet processing, PMEGP for manufacturing micro-enterprise, Karnataka 50% millet processing subsidy, Raitha Siri for raw material security, Stand-Up India for women entrepreneur collateral-free loan

capital_and_financing.recommended_funding_pathway: Small scale: Own 10% Rs 1.02 lakh + PMFME 35% subsidy up to Rs 10 lakh (Rs 2.97 lakh on 8.5 lakh) + bank loan 55% Rs 4.67 lakh; Alternatively Karnataka millet subsidy 50% up to 10 lakh reduces loan. For women SHG: Stand-Up India composite loan Rs 10 lakh-1 crore collateral-free via CGFSIL + PMFME seed capital Rs 40000 per member max 4 lakh per federation. Use NABARD FT-CFC Kalaburagi for free training reducing skill cost.
capital_and_financing.important_distinction: Business investment (Rs 8.5 lakh small) and government-scheme own contribution (10% under PMFME vs 50% under Karnataka 50% subsidy vs 5% under PMEGP women rural) are different concepts. Total investment includes machinery+infra+RM; own contribution is promoter equity; loan = investment - subsidy - own contribution.

data_quality.verification_summary: Major factual claims were checked against cited government and institutional sources - PIB PMFME 35% ceiling 10 lakh, PIB Millets Conclave Rs 10 lakh at 50% subsidy for millet processing machinery, REMSL APMC Gulbarga Bajra/Jowar commodities, NDMA DDMP Kalaburagi climate 5-45C rainfall 842mm, Selco Foundation jowar area 100482 ha production 134829 tonnes, March of Karnataka Dec 2023 50% subsidy up to 10 lakh, NABARD-CFTRI MoA FT-CFC 7 districts including Kalaburagi, Aland Bhootai and Jewargi FPCs via watershed.karnataka.gov.in and ICAR. Financial projections and taluk scores are explicitly labelled Calculated, Estimated, or Inferred where not directly reported by authoritative source.
